title: The Unofficial Mixtape
premise: Theo Coldharbour has spent twelve years as the careful, invisible statistician for her school's championship show-choir program, tracking every note and score while hiding the truth that she once sang — and froze — on this same stage as a child. When the senior college essay prompt demands one unvarnished truth, her answer accidentally goes public through the team's shared drive, exposing her past and fracturing the found family she's hidden inside. As the final audition approaches, Theo must choose between the safety of the numbers and the risk of her own voice, ultimately taking the stage herself — not to win, but to finally be seen — and discovering that the family she built will hold even when the labels come off.
about_author: Tamsin Halloran is a former show-choir accompanist who spent a decade backstage watching teenagers become themselves in real time. She writes stories about the kids in the wings, and lives in a coastal town where the high school auditorium still smells like hairspray and ambition.

chapters.title: The Numbers Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. She opens senior year running stats for the Northgate Voices, predicting competition scores to the decimal, and introduces her system of careful invisibility. When the college counselor hands out the essay prompt — 'Tell one truth you've never told' — Theo writes hers and locks the file. Emotional beat: the comfort and suffocation of control.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Almost
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, flashback-woven. We learn she was a child soloist who froze mid-song on the Northgate stage, after which her mother left and Theo swore off performing forever. She catalogs the team like a scientist: diva lead Priya, anxious tenor Marcus, choreo captain Dez. Beat: grief disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Shared Drive, Shared Secrets
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya finds Theo's essay draft in the team's shared drive while hunting for set-list notes and reads one line before guilt stops her: 'I used to be the girl who sang.' She says nothing, but starts watching Theo differently. Beat: the first crack in Theo's armor, seen from outside.

chapters.title: The Mixtape Rule
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The team's tradition: seniors make an unofficial mixtape of the songs that made them. Theo has made one every year and played it for no one. Marcus catches her listening and asks to hear it; she deflects with statistics. Beat: longing versus self-protection.

chapters.title: Regionals by the Decimal
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Regionals: Theo's projections say they'll win by 2.3 points if they cut Marcus's solo. Director Voss makes the cut; Marcus is gutted, and Theo realizes her numbers hurt the people she loves. Beat: the cost of objectivity.

chapters.title: What Priya Knows
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confronts Theo gently with what she read, expecting anger; instead Theo lies, cold and complete. Priya backs off but tells Dez something is wrong with their statistician. Beat: the loneliness of being known halfway.

chapters.title: The Essay Goes Public
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A syncing error pushes Theo's full essay to the entire team's drive — and someone screenshots it. By lunch, the truth is out: Theo Coldharbour was the girl who froze. The team's reactions split between curiosity and cruelty. Beat: exposure, the thing she built twelve years to avoid.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus, burned by the solo cut, finds the essay and feels the sting of hypocrisy — Theo predicted his failure and hid her own. He posts the screenshot to the team group chat 'so everyone knows who runs the numbers.' Beat: hurt weaponized.

chapters.title: Voss's Office
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Director Voss, who coached the child Theo, reveals she's known all along and offers her the understudy slot for the final audition — no promises, just a door. Theo refuses. Beat: the offer she isn't ready to take.

chapters.title: The Silent Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Rehearsal without Theo's voice in the booth falls apart; the team realizes how much they leaned on her. Dez, who froze once too — as a dancer — quietly leaves an old practice-room key in Theo's bag. Beat: found family showing up without being asked.

chapters.title: Practice Room B
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Alone in Practice Room B at midnight, Theo plays her mixtape and sings one verse to an empty room — the first time in twelve years. Priya, there for the same reason, hears her and says nothing, just harmonizes from the doorway. Beat: the thaw.

chapters.title: Marcus's Apology, Sort Of
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus learns his screenshot fueled a week of mockery, and that Theo's projection was right — his solo was the weak link. He apologizes badly, then honestly, and asks why she never told them. Beat: accountability and the beginnings of repair.

chapters.title: The Rigged Game
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo digs into competition data and discovers the circuit's judging has been quietly biased against small programs like theirs for years — the game really is rigged. She has proof that could burn it all down or protect the team. Beat: righteous anger meets strategic fear.

chapters.title: Going Public, Twice
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Theo presents the bias evidence to the team; Priya argues they should go public, Voss argues it will sink their season. The vote splits, and Priya realizes Theo would rather fight the system than stand on any stage. Beat: the team choosing its shape.

chapters.title: What My Mother Heard
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo visits her estranged mother, who reveals she left after the freeze not from shame but because she couldn't watch Theo disappear into 'careful.' She plays an old voicemail of six-year-old Theo singing. Beat: the memory that started everything, reframed.

chapters.title: The Withdrawal
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Reeling from the essay fallout and the judging scandal, Voss considers withdrawing from finals. The team faces losing the season they built together. Dez puts her own name in for the audition slot Theo refused. Beat: stakes crystallize.

chapters.title: The Mixtape, Played Aloud
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo plays her twelve years of mixtapes for the team in the black-box theater — one song per year, each a truth she never said. No speeches. When it ends, Marcus stands and adds a track of his own. Beat: the found family made audible.

chapters.title: Understudy
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya withdraws her own audition slot and hands it to Theo — 'not as charity, as strategy; you're our best voice and everyone knows it now.' Theo has twenty-four hours to decide. Beat: the door reopened by the people she lied to.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo rewrites her college essay one last time — not the safe truth but the whole one — and sends it. She rehearses alone, freezes once, and keeps going, learning the freeze is survivable. Beat: terror metabolized into readiness.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Finals day, mid-scandal, half-empty house. Dez performs first and dedicates it to 'the girl in the booth.' Then Theo walks out from the wings, takes the mic, and sings — voice shaking, then steady — while the team watches from the wings where she lived for twelve years. Beat: the climax; the freeze broken in public.

chapters.title: Score Revealed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The biased judging panel scores them unfairly anyway — but the bias evidence goes public the same night, and the circuit suspends the panel. The team doesn't win the trophy; they win something louder: the story, the apology, the next season's rules rewritten. Beat: victory redefined.

chapters.title: Track One
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue. At graduation, the seniors hand the underclassmen their mixtapes, and Theo records a new first track — her own voice, unhidden. Her college essay comes back with one handwritten note: 'Finally.' Beat: identity chosen, family kept, memory reclaimed.
